title: incident-bot: lightweight diagnostic toolbelt + ephemeral debug sessions for responders
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: on-call responders repeatedly run the same set of manual diagnostics when an alert fires (span tailing, recent-error log windows, lightweight heap/alloc snapshots, and quick-curl checks). This PR introduces a compact 'diagnostic toolbelt' exposed by incident-bot and an ephemeral debug session mode that lets responders run short-lived, auditable diagnostics without escalation to infra. Goals: reduce MTTD by providing one-click diagnostics, keep operations safe via TTLs and RBAC checks, and ensure cost caps through soft quotas and telemetry. What this change does: 1) Adds a new /v1/incidents/{id}/toolbelt API surface that aggregates a configurable set of diagnostics (logs tail, span tail, recent-errors, quick-rerun of failing healthcheck endpoints, and a heap-lite snapshot request). 2) Implements ephemeral debug sessions: a generated session token with a 15-minute TTL that grants scoped read-only access to targeted logs/traces and a sandboxed runner to perform pre-approved diagnostic commands. Sessions are recorded to the audit log and emit a session lifecycle event for billing/telemetry. 3) New UI affordance: a Toolbelt button in the incident timeline that opens the toolbelt panel (web/src/components/toolbelt/*) and a compact modal for ephemeral session creation with an estimated cost meter. 4) CLI helpers: incident-botctl toolbelt start --incident <id> --profile quick-check that opens a short-lived session and prints the session token and telemetry link. 5) Safety and Governance: RBAC checks against SSO groups, KMS-wrapped session secrets, per-tenant soft quotas, request rate-limiting, and a conservative whitelist of allowed runner commands. 6) Observability: new metrics (toolbelt.sessions.created, toolbelt.diagnostics.count, toolbelt.session.duration) and tracing spans to measure tool impact on latency/free resources. Implementation notes: backend changes in cmd/api/handler_toolbelt.go and internal/toolbelt/* which provide the orchestration, session manager, and audit plumbing; UI changes in web/src/components/toolbelt and web/src/styles; lightweight runner implemented as a new containerless job executor (internal/runner/lightweight) that runs commands in a hardened sandbox (no outbound network by default except to whitelisted endpoints). Diffs intentionally keep payloads small; large log downloads are paginated and pre-signed links have a short expiry. Testing: unit tests added for session lifecycle and RBAC checks (internal/toolbelt/session_test.go), e2e harness extends incident-sim to validate TTL expiry and audit log entries (test/e2e/toolbelt_flow.yaml). Migration and rollout: feature gated behind a runtime flag INCIDENT_TOOLBELT_ENABLED false by default; small canary rollout to 10% of orgs for first week with debug logging; telemetry hooks added to detect anomalous usage patterns and auto-disable soft-quotas if hit. Rollback plan: flip INCIDENT_TOOLBELT_ENABLED off, invalidate active sessions via session manager kill-all, and remove UI button via a targeted client config flag. References: ENG-4127 (design doc), ENG-4198 (safety review), and an internal runbook template updated to include toolbelt guidance.

review_comments: Jordan Blake: Looks good overall but we need a stronger guarantee that the runner cannot make data exfiltration requests. Please add egress deny-by-default and an allowlist at the tenant-level.
Aisha Kaur: Added deny-by-default egress rule and tenant-level allowlist; updated tests to assert egress blocked for disallowed domains.
Lina Perez: Suggest adding a UI indicator for session scope (what resources are accessible) before creating a session. Also request a telemetry event for cancelled sessions.
Aisha Kaur: Added scope summary to the modal and emit toolbelt.session.cancel events; updated docs with the scope table.
Marcus Chen: e2e flake observed on session expiry; looks like clock skew causes premature TTL failures in test infra. Please add clock-sync tolerance in the test harness.
Aisha Kaur: Increased tolerance to 5s in e2e harness and retried; CI green.
ci_checks: ci/e2e: pass (flaky run fixed on rerun)
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals from Jordan and Lina. Small follow-ups tracked in ENG-4251 (UI polish) and ENG-4260 (runner instrumentation). Release note: Added an on-call diagnostic toolbelt and ephemeral debug sessions for incident responders, gated by feature flag and tenant quotas.
release_notes: On-call diagnostic toolbelt (incidents UI & API): one-click diagnostics including log tail, span tail, quick health checks, and lightweight heap snapshots.
Ephemeral debug sessions: short-lived, auditable sessions for responders with TTL, RBAC, and quotas.
Feature is gated behind INCIDENT_TOOLBELT_ENABLED and rolled out to 10% of orgs initially.
